rules: Stage 10 backend_legacy_inventory.json is an immutable audit baseline; completed migrations are recorded here instead of rewriting history.
A removed source must have zero active hook, HTTP, Python-import and runtime consumers.
The canonical Door Cutting Order DocType base must remain because Frappe requires the active override to subclass it.
Public compatibility routes remain preserved until their route contract is explicitly retired.
A Stage 11 discovery that was not enumerated in the Stage 10 audit must be recorded explicitly with evidence before removal.

migrations.name: Retired alternate Door Cutting Order controller chain
evidence: hooks.py activates only DoorCuttingOrderController, which subclasses the canonical DoorCuttingOrder DocType controller directly.
The active save path delegates to process_order_save and FrappeDoorCuttingOrderSaveGateway rather than the alternate controller chain.
The active costing owner is FrappeOrderCostingAdapter and the active plan owner is FrappeOrderPlanAdapter/FrappeCutDimensionPlanAdapter.
PlanDoorCuttingOrder inherited CostingDoorCuttingOrder, which inherited the already-retired alternate controller branch; neither class is the Frappe override.
Architecture contracts reject PlanDoorCuttingOrder, CostingDoorCuttingOrder, DomainDoorCuttingOrder, TextBoardDoorCuttingOrder and FastDoorCuttingOrder from the active controller.
The Stage 11 contract scans runtime Python sources and rejects imports or symbol references to the complete removed chain.

migrations.name: Migrate runtime cutting imports to canonical Domain
evidence: The canonical Door Cutting Order base now imports expand_piece_groups, optimize_plan, round_value and validate_plan directly from domain.cutting.

The runtime import scan exposed exactly three additional consumers: performance_service.py, production_settings_service.py and remnant_planning.py; each was migrated without changing call signatures or algorithms.
Per-file Git compare confirmed the three service migrations are import-only changes.
Static architecture scans reject any runtime import of the three compatibility module paths.
Compatibility facades remain thin and available for historical/external Python import stability; their removal is intentionally not part of Batch 2.

migrations.name: Split Cutting Plan snapshot persistence from lifecycle compatibility
evidence: Cutting Plan snapshot creation, approval, and production freeze persistence moved to cutting_plan_snapshot_service.py without changing the persisted fields, validation flow, costs, status updates, or plan-source behavior.
drawing_approval_service.py now imports lock_order_for_production from the focused snapshot owner instead of the historical mixed service.

cutting_plan_service.py is now a thin compatibility facade: historical Python names delegate to the snapshot owner and historical whitelisted lifecycle methods delegate to their capability-protected canonical services.
The compatibility facade contains no frappe.new_doc, plan.insert, frappe.db.set_value, or Cutting Plan persistence logic.

Static contracts moved product-scope, special-shape geometry, production approval, and documentation/price assertions to the focused snapshot owner while retaining compatibility assertions on the old facade.
